howToCalculate.title: How to calculate a 100% CDI return
howToCalculate.p1: The calculator applies the daily CDI rate to the entered percentage, such as 100% or 110%, and compounds it by the number of business days.
howToCalculate.p2: The term in calendar days defines the estimated IR and IOF brackets; business days define yield compounding.

percentages.title: What 90%, 100%, or 110% of CDI means
percentages.p1: An investment at 100% of CDI uses the full CDI rate in the simulation. At 110%, the daily rate used is multiplied by 1.10.
percentages.p2: Higher percentages increase the yield estimate, but they are not advice and do not compare risk, liquidity, fees, or contracts.

currentCdi.title: Current CDI used by the calculator
currentCdi.p1: The default assumption uses an official Central Bank snapshot with observation on 2026-07-02: daily CDI of 0.052531% and annual CDI of 14.15%.
currentCdi.p2: The tool does not fetch live data in the browser. Use manual CDI mode if you want to test your own annual assumption.

taxes.title: IR and IOF on CDI-linked investments
taxes.p1: The estimate applies regressive IOF for redemptions up to 30 calendar days, based on the annex to Decree 6.306/2007.
taxes.p2: IR uses the regressive brackets from Law 11.033/2004: 22.5%, 20%, 17.5%, or 15%, depending on calendar-day term.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.p1: This tool is an educational estimate based on a dated official CDI rate or a rate entered by you. It does not recommend products, issuers, brokers, or investment decisions.
disclaimer.p2: Check the contract, taxation, liquidity, guarantees, fees, and official sources before investing.

q1.question: Does the calculator use the current CDI?
q1.answer: It uses a dated official Central Bank snapshot, with source sv=2026-07-06 and BCB observation of 2026-07-02. There is no live browser fetch.

q2.question: How do I calculate 100% of CDI?
q2.answer: Enter 100 in the % of CDI field. The calculator applies the daily CDI rate, compounds by business days, and estimates IR and IOF by calendar term.

q3.question: What changes at 110% of CDI?
q3.answer: The investment daily rate is 10% higher than the CDI rate used in the simulation. Taxes still follow the calendar-day term.

q4.question: Does the result already deduct IR and IOF?
q4.answer: Yes. The tool estimates IOF first when applicable, then IR on the remaining positive yield.

q5.question: Can I use it for LCI, LCA, funds, or Tesouro Selic?
q5.answer: Not as a final rule. Each product can have its own taxes, fees, liquidity, and rules; the calculator models a generic taxable CDI-linked application.

q6.question: Why can business days differ from calendar term?
q6.answer: CDI compounds on business days, while IR and IOF use calendar days. The estimate uses 252 business days per year and does not include a holiday calendar.

q7.question: Is the result investment advice?
q7.answer: No. The result is educational and does not evaluate products, issuers, liquidity, risk, guarantees, fees, or suitability.
